P1.evidence: No setter suffix on the title and no application read-back, so P1a does not apply. The four-part frame and the 'does that work?' agreement were never set — the call went from a camera-and-driving exchange straight into discovery. The open question did land: 'so Carl walk me through like what brought you to us, what's been going on, what's the main thing you're trying to fix'.

P2.evidence: Age arrived only because the prospect volunteered it — 'I mean, I'm 69 years old' — and the rep never asked age, height or weight, which scores a miss under the volunteered-information rule. Work was asked properly: 'are you still working?' then 'Is your work mostly sanitary or you move around too?'. Injuries were asked directly: 'Do you feel any stiffness or any injuries that you have from the past that are arising right now?'. Health conditions were only touched obliquely through 'Is your dad still alive?' and the father's lung cancer, which functioned as rapport rather than screening. Training week was half-covered — kettlebell history and resistance bands were asked, actual days trained were not. Diet was asked cleanly. Results from current training, sleep and daily energy were never raised at all.

P3.evidence: The surface question ran — 'is there anything in terms of fitness you're trying to achieve or are you wanting to change?' — producing 'I want to get more cut, lose a little bit of fat in the stomach'. Nothing below the surface was worked. There was no mobility/strength/energy fork, no 'something you want to do but can't', no 'outside of the physical, what's actually driving this', and no reflect-back. Family impact was gestured at rather than asked: the rep learned about ten grandchildren and said 'that ticks another box, why you need to be in shape', and asked 'Are you dating actively?', but never asked who the change impacts or what it does for him. The deep why never surfaced, which is why the think-about-it landed on nothing.

P4.evidence: Phase 4 was not attempted. The prospect said 'I've looked at a lot of programs' at 00:22:03, twenty-two minutes in and after the price, which was the only moment past attempts came up — and even then the rep asked what he was comparing on rather than what he had tried and why it had not stuck. No root cause, no gap named, no 'why can't you stick to it on your own'.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame of any kind. The nearest thing is the prospect's own line about not wanting to be 'one of those old guys that succeed and just give up', which he volunteered and the rep answered with agreement — 'You're the best evidence of that' — instead of building the two-year cost of inaction on top of it. Nothing was made real, nothing was settled for, no line in the sand.

P6.evidence: No commitment check before presenting. The rep moved from the three pillars directly to 'How do you feel about that?' and the prospect answered 'I just get to the pricing', which the rep accepted and priced immediately. Neither the belief question nor the 'any reason you wouldn't go all in' question was asked, so the price landed without a verbal yes underneath it — the exact failure mode the phase exists to prevent.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted — 'if you would have to make the decision right now, how do you feel?' — so the phase applies. Nothing in it ran. No payment was collected, the Trevor onboarding call was described conditionally rather than scheduled ('when you say yes today, we get the payment and everything, I will get you on call with him, probably even tomorrow, I would need to check his availability'), and the agreement email, Skool link and onboarding questionnaire were never mentioned.

objection_plays.detail: Two scripted moves landed in substance: the isolate ('if you would have to make the decision right now, how do you feel?') and the surfacing question ('So what do you need to think about actually?'). Everything after that was dropped — no 'do you feel what we've gone through CAN get you to your goal', no 'what makes you feel it can', no 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', no 'when do you make a different decision', no final 'are you sure, nothing else keeping you from being 100% in'. The rep took the third repetition as settled and went to the calendar.

'So let me just talk to my girlfriend and stuff' is OB in substance. The rep answered with a joke — 'Oh, don't bring your girlfriend into this. It's all about you, man.' — which got a laugh and closed the topic. None of the six scripted moves ran: no money-aside belief question, no 'what obstacles might come up', no 'is there any reason she would NOT want you stronger', no ownership question, no deposit-and-refund fallback.

Money surfaced twice — the prospect's reaction to the monthly figure at 00:20:59 (transcribed as 'Bye $1,000 a month is my big deal') and his 'No, I'm just saying it's $6,000 a month, basically', which reads as him mis-hearing the structure. Neither was isolated and no part of the financial picture sequence was run — no cash on hand, no monthly surplus, no cards, no available credit, no investments. The mis-hearing was also never corrected.

'I want to think with this vacation thing' is OD. The rep ran one adjacent move well — the programme-is-built-for-travellers reframe with the Europe/US startup client as proof, plus the 30-to-40-minute and app-travels-with-you specifics. But no scripted move ran: no 'things never slow down, when does it actually become the right time', no cost-of-delay, no 'the only thing you can control is right now'. The rep had also already conceded that the July 9th departure was a real constraint by promising a Trevor call within 24 hours, which weakened the reframe.

No fear or doubt objection surfaced. The prospect's hesitation was deliberation and comparison shopping, not apprehension about the modality — he was affirmatively keen on it ('I think that the Cowbell routines would be much more fun and different and harder').

Script gap. 'I've looked at a lot of programs. I just want to make sure this is what I want to do' is a comparison-shopping objection from a prospect who already owns a fully equipped gym and writes his own programming — his no-cost alternative is genuinely functional. The playbook has no play for this; it only anticipates capacity to pay. The rep asked the right opening question ('when you're comparing it to the other programs, what are actually looking for?') and then had nowhere to take the answer.

notes: The prospect asked for price at 18 minutes and the rep gave it, skipping Phases 4, 5 and 6 entirely — so three objections landed on a call with no root cause, no consequence and no commitment underneath them, and all three had to be handled cold. The coachable moment is the pillars-to-price jump: when a buyer says 'I just get to the pricing', the commitment check is what should follow, not the number.
